maudhui: (1) After Parliament has been dissolved or upon the occurrence of any other event referred to in subarticle (2) of Article 38 which necessitates an election of the President, every political party wishing to participate in the presidential election shall submit to the Electoral Commission the name of one of its members as a candidate for the office of President and the name of another member as a candidate for the office of Vice-President. (2) The nominations of candidates shall be submitted to the Electoral Commission on the day and at the time appointed in accordance with the law. (3) Where only one candidate is nominated, the Electoral Commission shall submit his name to the people who shall vote for or against him. (4) The election of the President shall be held on a day appointed by the Electoral Commission. (5) All other matters concerning the procedure for the election of the President shall be as prescribed by law. (6) A candidate shall be declared elected President if he has obtained a majority of the votes cast. (7) Where a candidate has been declared elected by the Electoral Commission, no court shall have jurisdiction to inquire into the election of that candidate.
